text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed sharply higher as speculators bought heavily amid positive technical indicators and a threatened strike by state workers in Colombia. March added $45 to close at $1,588 per tonne, while May closed $55 higher at $1,600 per tonne. In New York arabica futures came in slightly lower but within minutes soared sharply higher. Much of the buying was speculative and fund oriented with only minimal participation by the trade. News of another strike in Colombia gave the market its jolt today as did the realization that Colombia's 1996/97 coffee crop could be 2 to 3 million bags lower than expected. On top many players expect a lower Brazilian 1997/98 crop as well as reduced Central American crops in 1996/97. March added 7.60 cents/lb to close at 158.65 cents/lb, while May rose by 8.45 cents/lb to close at 154.45 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 6.00 and 8.05 cents/lb.

COLOMBIA - Colombian armed forces are on alert ahead of a threatened strike on Tuesday which promises to be the largest in 20 years. Talks between union chiefs and government ministers aimed at averting the indefinite stoppage by more than 800,000 state workers broke down in the early hours of Sunday. Much of Colombia's public administration is set to be paralyzed by the indefinite strike raising concern among some coffee exporters that shipments could be delayed.

PAPUA NEW GUINEA - Coffee production in Papua New Guinea could rise to 1.5 million bags by the year 2000, up from 1.1 million bags expected for 1996/97 (April/March) official sources said. It was added that the growth in output in the next few seasons will be due to a combination of higher yields and increased planting area.

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings totalled approximately 400,000 60-kg bags for the week ended February 1, up from 330,000 bags the previous week and compared with 330,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 1.865 million bags versus 1.810 million bags the same year ago period, it was added.

FRANCE - France imported 518,120 bags of coffee in November 1996, 6.6 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 6.195 million bags, 6.10 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 fell by 5.46 percent to 6.246 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Ivory Coast (730,300 vs 709,100 bags), Uganda (498,200 vs 381,500 bags), Brazil (682,100 vs 821,800 bags) and Colombia (511,700 vs 492,800 bags). The country exported 1.093 million bags of coffee in January/November 1996, nearly 12 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 fell by 7.4 percent to 1.074 million bags.
